findings.title: Require complete, case-bound restoration and amplitude records before accepting characterization
findings.problem: The answered-case restoration check compares e.fp_before to e.fp_after without requiring either field. Deleting both fingerprint tokens from the existing healthy scripted end row makes nil==nil and the case is still accepted as restored with a success summary. Session rows are collected by prefix with last-row-wins semantics: duplicates or a foreign case i are accepted, and the row i is never checked. Child amplitude words use %x+ rather than the real serializer eight-digit %08x, so a truncated post-call word can be accepted as an IEEE word. Current guards cover changed fingerprints and missing call/end rows, but miss these concrete incomplete/misassociated records.
findings.impact: The preparation gate can accept incomplete restoration evidence or attribute another case session row to this case, while claiming it rejected incomplete cases and preserved complete IEEE amplification observations. This is a witness integrity defect, not a demonstrated defect in the unchanged ambient routine.
findings.requested_change: Require both restoration fingerprints with their exact16hex-digit grammar before equality; require exactly one session row with the current case index and a valid0/1 session-unchanged field; require each sound-child word to have the actual8hex-digit grammar (preserve explicit na only for the declared nonsound case). Add finite real-driver controls that remove both fingerprints, duplicate/misindex the session row and truncate a post-call amplitude word, while retaining the existing genuine anomaly reporting and refused-case distinction. No amplitude oracle, extra trace framework or production change is required.
findings.support: Direct source control-flow analysis; no synthetic control or native runtime was executed by reviewer.
